newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CREDIT OUTLOOK - Rangebound ahead of supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CREDIT OUTLOOK - Rangebound ahead of supply.

text.p: U.S. credit markets will likely remain rangebound Tuesday as players digest some second-tier data and gear up for fresh Treasury supply.

"This week will be very technical, very supply driven, which means we're not real bullish on the next couple of days because supply is the only thing staring you in the face," said Patrick Dimick, economist at C.S. First Boston.
The U.S. Treasury will offer some $18.25 billion in two-year notes on Tuesday. The auction's bidding deadline is set for 1300 EDT/1700 GMT.
Analysts said moderate demand for the notes is seen.
"I'd be very surprised to see this two-year auction (yield) come in any worse than 5.95 percent," Dimick said.
"It could cheapen up a little bit between now and tomorrow's deadline, but I'd be very surprised if we broke through support at the 5.95 percent area," Dimick added.

In late when-issued trade on Monday, the two-year notes changed hands 5.9125 percent. Analysts said talk of possible heavy foreign central bank bidding may provide underpinning to the sale. "There has been talk in the market about central banks bidding," said a trader at a foreign investment bank.

Market players will also take in import and export prices for September at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT. Federal budget data are also expected to be issued Tuesday, although some analysts did not discount the possibility of a delayed release.
In a Reuters poll, U.S. economists predicted the federal budget will show a $29.4 billion surplus in September against a $41.85 billion deficit in August.

"Maybe people will focus on that a little bit ... We will know exactely what the fiscal year did in terms of how much the deficit improved. So maybe the market will like that a little bit," Schaja said.
"They (the foreign central banks) have been active buyers of U.S. securities over the last few weeks," the trader added.

On the economic indicator front, the market will take in some fresh weekly retail data on Tuesday. The BTM/Schroders chain store index for the week ended October 19 is due out at 0900 EDT/1300 GMT. The Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook retail sales index is scheduled to be released at 1455 EDT/1855 GMT.

Analysts said the numbers were not supposed to be a threat to the market. "I don't think the numbers will be worrisome for the market," said Marilyn Schaja, economist at Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette.
Analysts said prices are expected to remain rangebound Tuesday, with the yield on the U.S. 30-year benchmark Treasury bond fluctuating between 6-3/4 percent and 6.90 percent.
The bellwether was down 3/32 at 99-9/32 in late Monday trade to yield 6.81 percent.
The Federal Reserve added reserves to the banking system Monday through three-day fixed system repurchase agreements, when federal funds were trading at 5-3/16 percent.
On Tuesday, the fed funds rate is seen opening at 5.25 percent, in line with the central bank's target.
